text: The core of acoustics lies in exploring the nature and characteristics of sound waves - sound waves, as a form of mechanical vibration, propagate through media (gases, liquids, solids). Their frequency range is extremely wide (ranging from subsonic waves at 0.0001 Hz to ultrasonic waves at 10¹² Hz), and different frequencies of sound waves have distinct application scenarios: Infrasound (<20Hz): Low-frequency vibrations generated by earthquakes and tsunamis, which can be used for disaster warning.Audible sound (20Hz - 20kHz): Sounds that humans can perceive, including language communication, music acoustics, and noise control.Ultrasound (>20kHz): Such as medical ultrasound imaging, industrial flaw detection, cleaning and disinfection, etc.Extra-ultrasound (>10⁹Hz): Used for microscopic structure research (such as surface acoustic wave sensors).
